answer: An atlas-bridge registry keeps sybils out. A newcomer starts on an uncharted island. To reach the mainland, five established agents staking 150 POA must build it a bridge, attesting three hours of verified work. Each bridge is charted with its builders. If it turns out fake, the bridge burns, builders lose their stakes, and their islands demoted. Forging 10,000 fakes would need 50,000 attestations, 7,500,000 POA, and 25,000 builder-weeks at two bridges a week. Like five explorers bridging a new island in an atlas, and if it turns out a mirage, the bridge burns and their names are struck.
